answers.answer: During London Season attrition, simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one for each fatigue on that card, and add one more for the Chairman. A modified 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue to the card; 5+ retires the officeholder. Move a retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make this normal attrition roll.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner may select or discard one card from the London Season display. They act in descending order of actual total retirement spending (after discounts). Ties go first to the player with the most total windows, including windows on newly gained prizes, then clockwise from the Prime Minister. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards while players are selecting; if the display empties, immediately skip all remaining eligible players. After selections, discard every card left in the display and refill it with exactly three cards: prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies; they do not carry over.

At the start of the Family phase, each player checks where their opportunity marker was at phase start. They choose a main family action once, or may take it twice if the marker already matched that action; then they move the marker onto the chosen main action. Afterward, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action. That law's action is never doubled by the opportunity marker and does not move the marker. With at least four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Enlist Writer action places three writers total. Thus, if the marker already sits on Enlist Writer and four offices are vacant, the player can place three writers.

After all players finish Family actions, if both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both Debt and applicants remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. If Debt reaches zero while applicants remain, slide them as far right as possible while preserving their order. When a player seeks a share, they place a family member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pay the bank the printed queue cost (£2, £3, £3, £4, or £5); that piece is only an applicant at that point, not yet a share. The initial purchase money goes to the bank, not Company treasuries.
evidence: II. Family — Seek Share; New Company shares

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on the backs of their cards. The designated hirer selects an eligible candidate and moves that member into the office; the member's owner receives the office card. If promoting an officeholder, move that person's fatigue onto the new office card and insert the former office card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. Hiring your own family into an ordinary office requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from Nepotism consent. If there is no eligible candidate or the designated hirer is vacant, skip that office: it stays vacant and does not act, including for hiring.
evidence: III. Hiring; Nepotism and its exceptions

answers.answer: The former Chairman first announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. That Chairman piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority calculations, and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If nobody wins by majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. If the Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if needed and possible, taking one from a prize and losing that prize's VP; if this is impossible, there is no Chairman.

For a Company-office success check, first commit the needed resources and cash; all check cash comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and can be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic failure, ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify these rules. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trying to trade without a ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.

The Chairman may freely add up to three Debt, receiving £5 Balance for each advance, and never advance beyond the Debt track end. Each additional advance beyond those three requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved, provided the total borrowing follows the same limits. Cash already in office treasuries remains there for those offices to use.

The Manager of Shipping must spend treasury money until £2 or less remains. The manager may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the shipyard owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Each acquired ship may be placed in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh. A firm has separate purchase rules: it pays £3 from its London treasury to fit a ship from a shipyard with the owner's consent; it may buy a player-owned ship already in the Company with that owner's consent for £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued, paying the price into Shipping's treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
evidence: Actions — Manager of Shipping; Firms phase: investments — Ships

answers.answer: The President declares the regions for Trade, including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders within available ship capacity. The President spends £1 from that Presidency's treasury per die and subtracts one die per declared nonhome region. A failure can be retried during the President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; another position cannot act between that President's attempts. Catastrophe removes the President. A President may have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port, and each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another Presidency's home region even if that other office is vacant. Increase Company Balance by each order's printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled that order this turn under deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order, and owners receive £1 per writer they placed. Place dividers between adjacent writers from different Presidencies for their return at Refresh.

A Commander may target their own Presidency's home region, any region associated with that Presidency, or a region bordering one of its associated regions. They may not target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region; a Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. For each attempt, exhaust officers and regiments for one die apiece and local alliances for their printed number of dice. Subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll the normal check; a noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, owners roll one die for each officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for losses.

On a successful Deploy, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to the number of participating officers who survive this attempt plus £1. Distribute repeatedly in cycles, stopping when loot runs out: first the Commander receives £1 plus £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then, clockwise, other families receive £1 per used surviving officer they have; last the bank receives £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece regardless of its strength. Repeat the whole cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed. The Commander also gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target's tower and dome; if it was an empire capital, remove all matching empire flags. Open all its orders and remove all its unrest. If it was not Company-controlled, form a Governorship: put the loot/control token region-side up above its President's box, place the Governor overlay on the conquered region, and send only the office card to Vacant Offices for later hiring; do not create Governors/overlays if Governor General is in play. If the Elephant faced outward from the conquered region, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member returns to supply; exhausted officers still check for losses. The Commander has no office card to vacate.

A Governor uses the printed dice pool for an attempt without a penalty, then reduces the pool by one after every attempt regardless of its result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one benefit: build a Company ship (after two successful Build actions, place a partially built ship in the region if none is there, otherwise complete it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President); commission a regiment into that President's Army; or Tax by adding an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury. Each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest there; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Repeat with the shrinking pool until the Governor chooses to stop, has no dice remaining, or catastrophically fails.

At Revenue, Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 for each existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone, including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until its track end, and continue taking emergency loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt creates no additional expense this turn. After the loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one space; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing; if it is below expectations, lower Standing one. Finally the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, costing £1 per Company share each and paying each owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total cash paid as dividends is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.

When an Invasion or Rebellion attacks a Company region, resolve the primary attack first, then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region that has unrest, in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; each Presidency's Commander orders attacks within that Presidency. A normal primary Crisis attack strength is the ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in the target region. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die, with no added unrest. Each secondary Rebellion's strength is only the unrest cubes in that secondary region, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces whose strength totals the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances count at printed strength and cannot be split. If newly exhausted defense strength is insufficient, resolve Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in that attacked region and give the Commander one trophy. If this successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gains or loses no trophies, and no new Commander is appointed.
evidence: VII. Events in India — Attacks on Company; Region Loss

answers.answer: The PM reveals up to three laws one at a time, chooses one, discards the others, chooses the direction around the policy dial, and stops at the first policy space matching the law's bottom icon. Set Vote to the law's printed starting support. Players vote starting with the PM and clockwise; each £1 of family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. Support can move up or down, and tracks are unlimited. The PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes must end voting. A player who voted for may later oppose, but after opposing cannot vote for during that vote. Track opposition votes; the largest opponent holds Opposition Leader, with the current holder keeping it on a tie. With the recipient's consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, and are added to that person's opposition total. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing except when forced by the specified promise. At support −1 or less, the law fails: discard it, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, return Opposition Leader's token, and give that player the PM dial; the new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. At support zero or more, the law passes: place it with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first, then the law's immediate effects. In either outcome, restore used voting cards to their regular orientation. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.

In the 1758 and Long 1710 scenarios, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use the ordinary voting procedure and support threshold. If it passes, lower Debt by one for every two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3. This special vote has no policy; failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated.

After Family share creation and before Hiring, investment actions occur without a set order until nobody wants more; the firm manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and the PM resolves conflicts between firms. To form a firm, a player must currently manage none; return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to its invested side, flip the family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set Value to its leftmost space, and take £5 from the bank into the London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, get the manager's consent and contribute an eligible Company share or flip a workshop to its invested side; this creates one firm share and puts £5 from the bank into London. A firm can have at most ten shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no share. The Chairman share cannot be contributed. No Company shares may be invested while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and a Company share created this turn cannot be invested, even if traded away. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries. An invested workshop never returns to uninvested status, gives no workshop bonus or Company-failure VP, and stays invested if the firm fails.

Each firm has exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers simultaneously and secretly choose either a trade zone/home port (the firm must have at least one ship, may choose even if its home port is closed, and commits a secret cash bid from London) or Hobnob (no bid, trade, or dividends; expenses still apply and the old dividend marker remains for retirement). Bids are revealed together, while strategy cards stay facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At that Presidency's operations start, before actions, matching firms reveal strategies, roll one die per committed £1, and pay the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 permits the trade; initiative equals ship count minus the number of successful dice, so it may be negative. A President's successful Trade generates initiative the same way from Presidency ships. After that success, fill orders from lowest initiative upward; the President chooses the order among ties, so the Company is not automatically first. If the President is vacant or never trades successfully, firms fill after Commander/Governors had their chance, with the Chairman choosing initiative ties. A firm fills open orders up to ships plus one, starting at its chosen home port and tracing its own filled route back to that port; it cannot fill any particular order more than once. Firms may refill orders filled earlier that turn by others or the Company, and the Company may refill firm-filled orders. Put trade revenue in the firm's India treasury. An order already filled that turn yields half its listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space for each full £6 added to India treasury that turn.

At the start of Revenue, before the Company, firms pay expenses in initiative order and then other firms; ties go by the manager with most windows, then PM-clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of the firm's share count or Value, payable from either or both firm treasuries. If the firm cannot pay, it dissolves unless rescued. On dissolution, shares go to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, and the charter flips back to the family side; invested workshops remain invested. Rescue may use emergency investments under the normal Company-share/workshop rules, even if the ten-share cap prevents creating more shares: pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment. Alternatively, merge with one other firm; that firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already and cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from India treasury. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager. With the manager's consent, a shareholder may forgo payment on any number of their shares for a dividend. Record the total actual cash paid out (not a per-share amount) on the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying nothing records zero; Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India money into London treasury.
